statement: Two-phase grid-guided 2-opt SA (Phase 1: stale pos[], unlimited seg, batch=300; Phase 2: exact pos[], seg≤20, batch=1000) scores ~72.2 for penalty-aware TSP (N=200K, 2s), a 2.7-point improvement over random swap SA (69.5). The key enabler is exact pos[] tracking in Phase 2 combined with GG=sqrt(N) grid for O(1) spatial neighbor lookup.
regime: Penalty-aware TSP, N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, x-sorted city input
mechanism: Grid-guided 2-opt finds spatially nearby city pairs in O(1) via grid cell lookup. Short segments (≤20) keep pos[] update at O(20) per accepted move, enabling high throughput. Phase 1's stale pos[] with unlimited segments provides coarse exploration; Phase 2's exact pos[] provides precise refinement. 80/20 2-opt/swap ratio balances exploitation (spatial structure) with exploration (random diversification).
applicability_bounds: Requires GG=sqrt(N) grid granularity. Coarser grids (sqrt(N/2) or less) destroy the spatial precision. Phase split at ~70% of time limit. Segment limit of 20 in exact-pos phase is hardware-dependent (balances O(seg) update cost vs move quality).
